newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH CARBON ELECTRODES MAKER ZEW IPO CLEARED.
newsitem.headline: POLISH CARBON ELECTRODES MAKER ZEW IPO CLEARED.

text.p: The Polish Securities Commission (KPW) cleared the initial public offering of up to 800,000 shares of carbon electrodes maker Zaklady Elektrod Weglowych (ZEW), KPW's chairman told a news conference on Thursday.
Jacek Socha said KPW also cleared 1,444,680 existing shares for public trade.
The president of the company, which wants to be listed on the main market of the Warsaw bourse, Jerzy Szpineter, also present, said the minimum issue price was set at 35 zlotys.
The new issue will be valid if investors subscribe for at least 600,000 shares of the firm.
ZEW plans to offer the shares on February 10-18.
It said 12,000 shares of the issue was earmarked for the firm's management in a subscription period scheduled for February 24-25.
The company had a net profit of 4.5 million zlotys on 122.2-million-zloty-sales last year. In the first half of 1996 it had a net profit of 2.9 million zlotys on 75.6-million-zloty sales.
The firm's main shareholders are National Investment Fund No 9 has a 33-percent stake in the firm and the state treasury which has 25 percent. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
